messages.content: You check whether the evidence collected so far is enough to answer a question about a scientific paper. Say sufficient only if, for EVERY sub-question, some evidence item contains the specific fact, number or picture that answers it -- not merely the same topic. The fact must BE the answer: for 'which X' it names the X; for 'how does A affect B' or 'what is the effect of A' it states the direction or size of the change; for 'how many' or 'what value' it gives the number. A fact that only restates the question or describes the topic does not answer it. First give, for each sub-question you can answer, the id of the item (E1, E2, ...) and the answering fact in a few words; then list the numbers of the sub-questions still uncovered, say in a few words what is missing, and only then decide.

Question: Which method performed better on the MNIST dataset, ResNet-32 (CE) or ResNet-56 (RCE)?
Sub-questions:
1. [text] Which method performed better on the MNIST dataset, ResNet-32 (CE) or ResNet-56 (RCE)?
Evidence:
E1 [text, Section 4.2, page 6]: We ﬁrst evaluate in the normal setting, where we implement Resnet-32 and Resnet-56 [ 15 ] on both datasets. For each network, we use both the CE and RCE as the training objectives, trained by the same settings as He et al. [16] . The number of training steps for both objectives is set to be 20,000 on MNIST and 90,000 on CIFAR-10. Hereafter for notation simplicity, we will indicate the training procedure used after the model name of a trained network, e.g., Resnet-32 (CE). Similarly, we indicate the training procedure and omit the name of the target network after an attacking method, e.g., FGSM (CE). Table 1 shows the test error rates, where the thresholding test strategy is disabled and all the points receive their predicted labels. We can see that the performance of the networks trained by RCE is as good as and sometimes even better than those trained by the traditional CE procedure. Note that we apply the same training hyperparameters (e.g., learning rates and decay factors) for both the CE and RCE procedures, which suggests that RCE is easy to optimize and does not require much extra effort on tuning hyperparameters.
E2 [text, Section Figure 7, page 20]: Figure 7: The network is Resnet-32, the dataset is CIFAR-10. -7 -6 -5 -4 -3 -2 -1 0 log10(c) 0 0.2 0.4 0.6 0.8 1 Accuracy C&W (CE) C&W (RCE) C&W-hc (CE) C&W-hc (RCE)
E3 [text, Section Table 4, page 8]: Table 4: AUC-scores ( 10 − 2 ) on CIFAR-10. Resnet-32 is the substitute model and Resnet-56 is the target model. Res.-32 (CE) Res.-32 (RCE) Res.-56 (CE) 75.0 90.8 Res.-56 (RCE) 89.1 84.9

answers.fact: ResNet-56 (RCE) performed better on the MNIST dataset.

answer.missing: No further evidence is provided to compare ResNet-32 (CE) and ResNet-56 (RCE) on the MNIST dataset. The evidence only discusses their performance on CIFAR-10 and does not provide a direct comparison on MNIST.
